prompt: Let $f(x) = 3x$ and $g(x) = x + 5$. Write $f(g(x))$ as a simplified expression.
hint: Instead of a number, the inside machine now hands over a whole expression: $g(x) = x + 5$.

hints.text: Instead of a number, the inside machine now hands over a whole expression: $g(x) = x + 5$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $f(x) = 2x$ and $g(x) = x + 1$. Then $f(g(x)) = 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2$. Same method: drop the inside expression into $f$, then distribute.
Feed the expression $x + 5$ into $f$, which triples its input, to get $3(x + 5)$. Then distribute the $3$.
Distributing gives $3(x + 5) = 3x + 15$, so the simplified form of $f(g(x))$ is $3x + 15$.

explanation: The inside machine $g$ turns $x$ into the expression $x + 5$.
The outside machine $f$ triples whatever it receives, so $f(g(x)) = 3(x + 5)$.
Distributing the $3$ over both terms gives the simplified answer $3x + 15$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with a number
steps: Run one number through both machines, say $x = 2$: $g(2) = 2 + 5 = 7$, and then $f(7) = 3 \times 7 = 21$.
The inside is tripled as a whole, so both the $x$ and the $5$ get tripled, which suggests $3x + 15$.
Test that expression with the same number: $3(2) + 15 = 21$, which matches the machines, so $f(g(x)) = 3x + 15$.
